name: v3.29.0
body:
- **LaTeX.** Vale now lints `.tex` files. It reads the source without running TeX, so a document that doesn't compile still lints. Math, citations, references, and verbatim text are treated as code; sections, captions, footnotes, list items, and table cells are prose.
- **Typst, built in.** typst2vast is now embedded, so Typst files need nothing else installed.
- **`IgnoredPaths`.** A new `.vale.ini` key for paths that are never linted, even when named on the command line.
- **Pinned packages.** A package can be pinned to its archive's digest.
- **`.yaml` rules.** Rules load from `.yaml` files as well as `.yml` (#1232, thanks @seragAhmed).

![A Markdown page, a Go file, and a YAML file sketched as bars, with the prose lit, the code and markup dark, and one alert in each at its exact position.](https://vale.sh/blog/og/spelling.png)

### [Spell checking is a parsing problem](https://vale.sh/blog/spelling)

Vale reads the format before it checks the spelling, so in fifteen markup formats, six programming languages, and three data formats, its output is the misspellings in your prose and nothing else. What that gets you, how fast it is, and how to bring a technical vocabulary along.
